_comment: Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 + its own 4-step Lightning LoRA. This REPLACES workflow 03 (2509 at 20 steps, 48 s). Deliberately uses the same input image and the same prompt as 03 so the two are directly comparable on both speed and quality.
_notes: WHY 2511 AND NOT 2509 + a Lightning LoRA: 2511 is a newer base model, not just a faster one. It mitigates image drift, holds character consistency better, has selected community LoRAs baked in, and is markedly better on multi-person and multi-image work. Buying the 2509 Lightning LoRA would have bought speed on an older base - the wrong trade.
steps=4 / cfg=1.0 is mandatory with the Lightning LoRA (node 4). Without the LoRA, 2511 wants steps=40 / cfg=3.0 - note that is 40, not the 20 that 2509 used.
shift=3.1 on ModelSamplingAuraFlow. 2509 used 3.0. Small, but it is what the 2511 template ships.
FluxKontextImageScale (node 8) snaps the input to a resolution the model likes. Do not skip it - off-grid input sizes cause soft or misaligned edits.

FluxKontextMultiReferenceLatentMethod with 'index_timestep_zero' (nodes 11/13) is required by 2511 even for a SINGLE reference image. Omit it and edits drift off the source. This is new versus 2509 and is the most common reason a 2509 graph 'stops working' when you swap the model in.
TextEncodeQwenImageEditPlus takes image1/image2/image3 - up to three references. See workflow 23 for the two-image case.
The negative encoder (node 12) still needs the same image wired in. An empty-image negative pulls the edit toward the mean and washes out the result.

inputs.prompt: Change the scene to deep winter: the rocks and the lighthouse are coated in thick snow and ice, the sea is slate grey with drifting ice floes, the sky is a cold pale overcast. Keep the lighthouse structure, its position and the camera angle exactly as they are.
